raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-ALB-CitizenServiceDelivery",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Weak procurement capacity at ADISA may cause delays, non‑compliance, and cost overruns.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Hire qualified procurement specialist, provide bank technical assistance, use sample TORs, and enforce close bank oversight of procurement processes.",
      "evidence": "Procurement risk rating is High. Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency. (Section 66)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Overall financial management risk is substantial due to limited experience of ADISA and MIPA with large donor‑funded operations.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Deliver targeted fiduciary training, adopt a detailed Financial Management Manual, hire finance specialists, and implement robust internal controls with bank supervision.",
      "evidence": "Overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial. ADISA and MIPA lack experience with large donor‑funded operations. (Section 62)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Ambitious timeline for constructing the central Citizen Service Center may be missed.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Create a realistic construction schedule with contingency buffers, monitor milestones regularly, consider PPP financing options, and secure timely approvals.",
      "evidence": "Central CSC building to be constructed in Tirana by first half of 2017; timeline described as very ambitious. (Section 7)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Lack of existing IT systems and fragmented registers hinder integration and achievement of Level 3 automation.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop a phased IT implementation plan, allocate resources for system development, enforce interoperability standards, pilot test services, and coordinate with NAIS for integration.",
      "evidence": "Seven institutions have no IT system; legacy registers are paper; integration required for Level 3 automation. (Section 10)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Bureaucratic resistance from ministries and staff may impede front‑office reforms and service redesign.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement a change‑management program, involve staff in redesign, provide training on new processes, communicate benefits, and create incentives for adoption.",
      "evidence": "Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back‑office functions; ministries may not welcome ceding front‑office function. (Section 58)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Delay in passing omnibus legislation needed for regulatory reforms could stall service re‑engineering.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Accelerate legislative drafting, set clear parliamentary timelines, engage legal experts, monitor progress, and prepare contingency measures for partial implementation.",
      "evidence": "Reform of government services will be implemented through omnibus legislation expected to be passed by end of 2016. (Section 19)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Construction of the CSC may cause dust, noise, waste and other environmental impacts.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Implement the Environmental Management Plan, enforce construction best practices, conduct regular site inspections, and maintain a community liaison for grievance handling.",
      "evidence": "Potential environmental impacts of new CSC construction include dust, noise, waste; mitigated by EMP. (Section 70)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Emphasis on digital services could marginalize poor and vulnerable citizens with low internet access.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Maintain non‑digital service points, provide assisted internet access, run targeted outreach campaigns, and ensure information is available via posters, call centres, and community centres.",
      "evidence": "Risk that focus on state‑of‑the‑art online services may diminish access of the poor and vulnerable due to low internet penetration. (Section 6)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Delay in recruiting procurement and administrative specialists for the PMU may weaken project implementation.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Fast‑track recruitment, use interim consultants if needed, define clear TORs, and obtain bank assistance for procurement support.",
      "evidence": "Procurement and Administrative Specialist positions have been readvertised; PMU staff not yet fully set up. (Section 66)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Results‑Based Financing disbursements are blocked until DLI#5 (strategic plan approval and baseline survey) is achieved.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize completion of the strategic plan and baseline survey, allocate dedicated resources, and provide technical assistance to meet DLI#5 on schedule.",
      "evidence": "No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved. (Section 31)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Complex coordination among multiple ministries, agencies, and inter‑ministerial committees may cause delays and misalignment.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish clear coordination mechanisms, regular steering‑committee meetings, assign a dedicated coordination officer, and use project‑management tools to track responsibilities.",
      "evidence": "Multiple inter‑ministerial committees and working groups; coordination among many agencies is required and may be complex. (Section 58)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "ADISA, as a newly created agency, has limited implementation experience and capacity.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide intensive capacity‑building, hire experienced managers, leverage technical assistance, and monitor performance against clear milestones.",
      "evidence": "ADISA created in Oct 2014; limited track record; capacity strengthening needed. (Section 41)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Improved service access may increase demand, creating budget pressures amid existing fiscal constraints.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct demand forecasting, adjust budget allocations, explore additional financing sources, and implement cost‑recovery where appropriate.",
      "evidence": "Improved access may increase demand for services, with budget implications; fiscal constraints noted. (Section 49)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "High levels of perceived corruption may persist, undermining public trust in the reform outcomes.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen anti‑corruption controls, enforce front‑office separation, monitor bribery reports via citizen feedback, and run public awareness campaigns.",
      "evidence": "Corruption remains high; 30% of citizens exposed to bribery; risk reforms may not fully reduce it. (Sections 1‑3)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Low response rate (≈22%) to the citizen feedback mechanism may limit data quality for performance monitoring.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Increase outreach, diversify feedback channels, offer incentives for participation, and supplement with periodic surveys to improve data completeness.",
      "evidence": "Citizen feedback mechanism response rate about 22%; limited data may affect performance monitoring. (Sections 40‑41)"
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Weak procurement capacity at ADISA may cause delays, non‑compliance, and cost overruns.
risks.mitigation: Hire qualified procurement specialist, provide bank technical assistance, use sample TORs, and enforce close bank oversight of procurement processes.
risks.evidence: Procurement risk rating is High. Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency. (Section 66)

risks.description: Overall financial management risk is substantial due to limited experience of ADISA and MIPA with large donor‑funded operations.
risks.mitigation: Deliver targeted fiduciary training, adopt a detailed Financial Management Manual, hire finance specialists, and implement robust internal controls with bank supervision.
risks.evidence: Overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial. ADISA and MIPA lack experience with large donor‑funded operations. (Section 62)

risks.description: Ambitious timeline for constructing the central Citizen Service Center may be missed.
risks.mitigation: Create a realistic construction schedule with contingency buffers, monitor milestones regularly, consider PPP financing options, and secure timely approvals.
risks.evidence: Central CSC building to be constructed in Tirana by first half of 2017; timeline described as very ambitious. (Section 7)

risks.description: Lack of existing IT systems and fragmented registers hinder integration and achievement of Level 3 automation.
risks.mitigation: Develop a phased IT implementation plan, allocate resources for system development, enforce interoperability standards, pilot test services, and coordinate with NAIS for integration.
risks.evidence: Seven institutions have no IT system; legacy registers are paper; integration required for Level 3 automation. (Section 10)

risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance from ministries and staff may impede front‑office reforms and service redesign.
risks.mitigation: Implement a change‑management program, involve staff in redesign, provide training on new processes, communicate benefits, and create incentives for adoption.
risks.evidence: Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back‑office functions; ministries may not welcome ceding front‑office function. (Section 58)

risks.description: Delay in passing omnibus legislation needed for regulatory reforms could stall service re‑engineering.
risks.mitigation: Accelerate legislative drafting, set clear parliamentary timelines, engage legal experts, monitor progress, and prepare contingency measures for partial implementation.
risks.evidence: Reform of government services will be implemented through omnibus legislation expected to be passed by end of 2016. (Section 19)

risks.description: Construction of the CSC may cause dust, noise, waste and other environmental impacts.
risks.mitigation: Implement the Environmental Management Plan, enforce construction best practices, conduct regular site inspections, and maintain a community liaison for grievance handling.
risks.evidence: Potential environmental impacts of new CSC construction include dust, noise, waste; mitigated by EMP. (Section 70)

risks.description: Emphasis on digital services could marginalize poor and vulnerable citizens with low internet access.
risks.mitigation: Maintain non‑digital service points, provide assisted internet access, run targeted outreach campaigns, and ensure information is available via posters, call centres, and community centres.
risks.evidence: Risk that focus on state‑of‑the‑art online services may diminish access of the poor and vulnerable due to low internet penetration. (Section 6)

risks.description: Delay in recruiting procurement and administrative specialists for the PMU may weaken project implementation.
risks.mitigation: Fast‑track recruitment, use interim consultants if needed, define clear TORs, and obtain bank assistance for procurement support.
risks.evidence: Procurement and Administrative Specialist positions have been readvertised; PMU staff not yet fully set up. (Section 66)

risks.description: Results‑Based Financing disbursements are blocked until DLI#5 (strategic plan approval and baseline survey) is achieved.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize completion of the strategic plan and baseline survey, allocate dedicated resources, and provide technical assistance to meet DLI#5 on schedule.
risks.evidence: No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved. (Section 31)

risks.description: Complex coordination among multiple ministries, agencies, and inter‑ministerial committees may cause delays and misalignment.
risks.mitigation: Establish clear coordination mechanisms, regular steering‑committee meetings, assign a dedicated coordination officer, and use project‑management tools to track responsibilities.
risks.evidence: Multiple inter‑ministerial committees and working groups; coordination among many agencies is required and may be complex. (Section 58)

risks.description: ADISA, as a newly created agency, has limited implementation experience and capacity.
risks.mitigation: Provide intensive capacity‑building, hire experienced managers, leverage technical assistance, and monitor performance against clear milestones.
risks.evidence: ADISA created in Oct 2014; limited track record; capacity strengthening needed. (Section 41)

risks.description: Improved service access may increase demand, creating budget pressures amid existing fiscal constraints.
risks.mitigation: Conduct demand forecasting, adjust budget allocations, explore additional financing sources, and implement cost‑recovery where appropriate.
risks.evidence: Improved access may increase demand for services, with budget implications; fiscal constraints noted. (Section 49)

risks.description: High levels of perceived corruption may persist, undermining public trust in the reform outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen anti‑corruption controls, enforce front‑office separation, monitor bribery reports via citizen feedback, and run public awareness campaigns.
risks.evidence: Corruption remains high; 30% of citizens exposed to bribery; risk reforms may not fully reduce it. (Sections 1‑3)

risks.description: Low response rate (≈22%) to the citizen feedback mechanism may limit data quality for performance monitoring.
risks.mitigation: Increase outreach, diversify feedback channels, offer incentives for participation, and supplement with periodic surveys to improve data completeness.
risks.evidence: Citizen feedback mechanism response rate about 22%; limited data may affect performance monitoring. (Sections 40‑41)
